chapter: Washington, New Orleans and the road
title: Mistaken for a Creole in Louisiana
summary: Patrons took him for Creole and spoke French; he insisted he was from Kansas City and his mother looked white.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x:
So I...I say, "I wanna see some Creoles."
"There's one, there's one, there's one, there's one, there's one."
"Appear to me them's half-white folks. 'At's all they are."
Say, "They don't call theyselves white...white folks. They Creoles. Ya talk French t' 'em."
So... Ever'body thought I was a Creole. So I talk...talk... be talkin' to me in that funny talk...that French talk. I didn't know what the devil they's talkin' about.
I say, "Talk English, man! Talk English, man. This America."
They think I gonna say some place in Louisiana. I say, "Kansas City, Missouri." That shocked 'em.
"You ain't from no Kansas City, Missouri. You stop lyin'."

Say, "Yes, I am." I say, "I know all about that...half-white folks... My mother looked like a white woman." I said, "She ain't from no Louisiana." I say, "In fact...in fact, if you walk up on her and see her, you'd...you'd be sure that she's a white woman. But she not. She my momma."
Say, "Well, she could be white woman if she is your momma."
I said, "Well, she look like white but she ain't." I say, "Y'all..." I say, "Her mother is part Indian." I say, "She don't look like no white woman." I say, "She's red like fire."
He say, "Well, I don't know. But you...strictly Louisiana dude."

I say, "Well, my daddy's from Louisiana." I say, "Maybe I picked it up from him. Maybe I look like him." I say, "But I know damned well I ain't from no Louisiana. I's born in Kansas City, Missouri. At least, what they told me."
I was kinda shocked. I say, I...now I got t' try to believe it myself. Cut it off [the tape recorder]."
